goal: Make `kitcode mini` open as the smallest practical always-on-top micro chip instead of the current large mini dashboard.

in: Replace the `/mini` HTML/CSS layout with a compact micro chip focused on break progress percent and status.
Resize the Electron BrowserWindow from the current large fixed mini window to an approximately 160x64 chip, not exceeding 180x80 by default.
Keep the chip always-on-top, frameless, movable, and draggable.
Keep the close control available in the micro layout without interfering with dragging.
Keep live updates using the existing `/api/summary` initial fetch and `/api/events` summary stream.
Show concise states for READY, LIVE, IDLE, OFFLINE, and reconnecting/error behavior.
Use the existing reward summary and milestone progress logic; do not change tracker, ledger, reward, or API behavior.
Allow the body of the chip to open the dashboard or another clear detail view while preserving the close button.
out: No changes to local state persistence under `~/.kitcode/state.json`.
No changes to reward calculation, tier thresholds, redemption logic, or equals counting.
No new backend or campaign claim flow.
No redesign of the full React dashboard.
No new CLI commands or command options unless implementation proves a tiny flag is unavoidable.
No expansion mode for the first version.

acceptance_criteria.summary: Electron mini window defaults to an approximately 160x64 chip and does not exceed 180x80.
`/mini` no longer renders the large ring, metric tiles, long status message, or `Mini.tsx` header.
The chip shows a progress percent plus a concise status label for LIVE, READY, IDLE, OFFLINE, and reconnecting/error states.
When any local reward tier has `status === "ready"`, the chip prioritizes the READY state visually and textually.
The chip remains draggable, the close button works, and clicking the chip body opens a clear detail destination without triggering close.
Implementation continues using existing `/api/summary` and `/api/events` data and does not alter local API or reward contracts.
At the chosen chip size, all labels fit without scrollbars, clipping, or incoherent overlap.

coverage_plan.summary: Run the CLI package build script after implementation so existing command, reward, snapshot, ledger, and syntax checks still pass.
Add or perform a focused smoke check that `/mini` HTML contains the micro chip controls and no longer contains the removed large layout elements.
Run `kitcode track` and `kitcode mini` locally, then verify chip size, drag, close, click behavior, and READY/LIVE/IDLE/OFFLINE text at runtime.

risks.summary: The current Electron window hard-locks minimum and maximum size to 340x430, so both BrowserWindow sizing and HTML body dimensions must change together.
risks.mitigation: Update `mini-electron.mjs` dimensions and remove/replace `mini-window.mjs` body min-width/min-height values in the same implementation.

risks.summary: A frameless draggable chip can conflict with clickable controls and dashboard-open behavior.
risks.mitigation: Use `-webkit-app-region: drag` on the shell and `no-drag` on close/click targets; keep click target behavior simple.

risks.summary: Removing time and equals details may feel sparse to users expecting the current mini dashboard.
risks.mitigation: Use the chip as a glance surface and make clicking it open the full dashboard/detail experience.

risks.summary: When Electron is unavailable, `/mini` opens in a normal browser tab where the chip layout should still look intentional.
risks.mitigation: Center the chip in larger browser viewports while preserving the micro dimensions for Electron.

implementation_handoff.summary: Transform the mini window from a large dashboard card into a micro always-on-top status chip.
suggested_sequence: Update Electron dimensions, min/max size, and placement margin for the micro chip.
Replace mini HTML/CSS with a tiny chip layout that uses system fonts, stable dimensions, no scroll, and compact status styling.
Keep or adapt existing progress calculation and EventSource update code while removing unused time/equals/message node updates.
Add chip body click behavior that opens a detail destination, while the close button remains separate.
Run syntax/build checks and perform a manual visual check of size, drag, close, click, and live state updates.
current_behavior_evidence: packages/kitcode-cli/src/mini-electron.mjs currently sets width 340, height 430, minWidth 300, minHeight 360, and locks minimum/maximum size.
packages/kitcode-cli/src/mini-window.mjs currently sets body min-width 320 and min-height 390 and renders a large progress ring, time/equal metric tiles, and a long message.
packages/kitcode-cli/src/api.mjs already serves `/mini`, `/api/summary`, and `/api/events`; no API expansion is needed.
notes: Use existing reward summary fields and ready tier detection.
Do not change persisted state or reward math.
Prefer concise labels over long copy because the selected target is the Micro 160x64 direction.

goal: Redesign `kitcode mini` from the current tiny 160x64 chip into a more polished fixed-size mini panel that is draggable, not resizable, and opens near the bottom-right of the desktop viewport without sitting too deep on the screen.

in: Resize the Electron BrowserWindow from the current 160x64 micro chip to a compact but readable mini panel, targeting approximately 300-320px wide and 136-156px tall.
Place the mini window at the bottom-right of the primary display work area by default, with enough right and bottom margin to avoid feeling clipped or too deep near the dock/taskbar.
Keep the mini window frameless, always-on-top, movable, draggable, and non-resizable.
Keep the close control available and ensure it does not conflict with window dragging.
Replace the micro chip HTML/CSS with a polished mini panel that clearly shows KitCode identity, progress percent, status, and a compact progress indicator.
Keep concise visual states for READY, LIVE, IDLE, OFFLINE, and reconnecting/error behavior.
Keep live updates using the existing `/api/summary` initial fetch and `/api/events` summary stream.
Use existing reward summary and milestone progress logic; do not change tracker, ledger, reward, local state, or API behavior.
Preserve body click behavior that opens the dashboard/detail destination while keeping close separate.
out: No user resizing, resize handles, or expanded layout mode in this version.
No changes to local state persistence under `~/.kitcode/state.json`.
No changes to reward calculation, tier thresholds, redemption logic, equals counting, or milestone contracts.
No new backend or campaign claim flow.
No redesign of the full React dashboard.
No new CLI commands or command options unless implementation proves a tiny flag is unavoidable.

acceptance_criteria.summary: Electron mini window defaults to a fixed compact panel around 300-320px wide and 136-156px tall, large enough to look intentional and readable.

The window opens near the bottom-right of the primary display work area with approximately 24-32px right margin and 64-88px bottom margin, instead of opening at the top-right or too close to the bottom edge.
The window remains draggable and movable but cannot be resized by the user; min and max dimensions match the selected panel size.
`/mini` renders a polished mini panel rather than the current 160x64 micro chip, with stable dimensions, KitCode identity, progress percent, status label, and a compact progress indicator.
When any local reward tier has `status === "ready"`, the panel prioritizes READY state visually and textually over LIVE or IDLE.
The panel shell remains draggable, the close button works without triggering drag or dashboard open, and clicking the main panel body opens the existing dashboard/detail destination.
At the selected fixed panel size, all labels, controls, and progress elements fit without scrollbars, clipping, layout shift, or incoherent overlap.
Implementation continues using existing `/api/summary` and `/api/events` data and does not alter local API, reward, ledger, tracker, or persistence contracts.

coverage_plan.summary: Run the CLI package build script after implementation so existing command, reward, snapshot, ledger, and syntax checks still pass.
Run syntax checks for the mini source files after changing the Electron placement and `/mini` HTML renderer.
Run `kitcode track` and `kitcode mini` locally, then verify bottom-right placement, fixed size, drag behavior, close behavior, dashboard-open click behavior, and READY/LIVE/IDLE/OFFLINE presentation.

risks.summary: The existing implemented active plan intentionally made the mini window a 160x64 micro chip, so this requirement reverses that UX decision.
risks.mitigation: Treat `comfortable-mini-window` as the newer product direction and update both Electron dimensions and `/mini` body dimensions together.

risks.summary: Bottom-right placement depends on the primary display work area and can feel different across macOS dock positions, Windows taskbars, and multi-monitor setups.
risks.mitigation: Use `screen.getPrimaryDisplay().workArea` and explicit bottom/right margins; keep the first implementation focused on primary display behavior.

risks.summary: A frameless draggable window can conflict with close and dashboard-open click targets.
risks.mitigation: Use `-webkit-app-region: drag` on passive shell/header areas and `-webkit-app-region: no-drag` on close and clickable content.

risks.summary: Adding more visual information than the micro chip can make the mini panel feel busy if the height stays too small.
risks.mitigation: Limit the panel to identity, status, percent, one compact progress bar, and one short hint line; defer metrics tiles and expanded details.

risks.summary: When Electron is unavailable, `/mini` may open in a normal browser tab where fixed panel dimensions should still look intentional.
risks.mitigation: Center the fixed mini panel in larger browser viewports while preserving Electron-sized dimensions.

implementation_handoff.summary: Transform the mini window from an overly small micro chip into a fixed-size, polished bottom-right mini panel while preserving existing local API and reward behavior.
suggested_sequence: Update Electron width and height to the selected compact panel size, keep `resizable: false`, and lock min/max size to those dimensions.
Move default placement from top-right to bottom-right using `workArea.y + workArea.height - height - bottomMargin`, with a larger bottom margin than right margin.
Replace the current chip CSS/HTML with a mini panel layout that uses stable fixed dimensions, no scroll, concise typography, a status pill, and a progress bar.
Keep the existing `getBreakProgress`, ready-tier detection, `/api/summary` fetch, and `/api/events` EventSource update path.
Apply drag/no-drag regions so passive shell/header areas move the window and interactive close/open controls remain clickable.
Run syntax/build checks and perform a manual visual check on desktop.
current_behavior_evidence: packages/kitcode-cli/src/mini-electron.mjs currently sets width 160, height 64, minWidth 160, minHeight 64, and locks minimum/maximum size to the chip dimensions.
packages/kitcode-cli/src/mini-electron.mjs currently sets `y` to `workArea.y + margin`, which places the mini window near the top-right rather than bottom-right.
packages/kitcode-cli/src/mini-window.mjs currently sets body min-width 160 and min-height 64 and renders a tiny chip with percent, status, hint, close, and grip.
packages/kitcode-cli/src/api.mjs already serves `/mini`, `/api/summary`, and `/api/events`; no API expansion is needed.
notes: Use existing reward summary fields and ready tier detection.
Do not change persisted state, tracker behavior, reward math, or API contracts.
Prefer a readable mini panel over a large dashboard card; do not restore metric tiles unless the selected size can support them without clutter.
Recommended initial dimensions are 320x148 with right margin 28 and bottom margin 72.

goal: Add `kitcode terminal` as a separate Electron terminal-style window that opens centered, can be dragged and resized freely, and provides a safe KitCode-only fake shell with English Vim-inspired UI.

in: Add a public `kitcode terminal` CLI command.
Make `kitcode terminal` check the local tracker before opening, using the same unavailable-tracker behavior as `dashboard` and `mini`.
Open a separate Electron BrowserWindow centered on the primary display work area by default.
Make the terminal window movable, draggable, and user-resizable with sensible minimum dimensions, similar to a native desktop terminal.
Serve a local terminal HTML view from the tracker, expected as `GET /terminal`.
Render an English-only terminal UI with a large Vim-inspired title treatment, such as `KITCODE TERMINAL`, a Vim-style status/tab line, command output history, and a focused prompt.
Implement a safe KitCode-only command engine for `help`, `status`, `summary`, `rewards`, `dashboard`, `mini`, and `clear`.
Use existing local summary and reward data for status, summary, and rewards output; do not add new persistence.
Support terminal basics: Enter submits, Up/Down navigates command history, `clear` clears output, and unknown commands return a helpful safe-shell message.
Open external dashboard/detail destinations through Electron-safe external opening behavior rather than arbitrary shell execution.
out: No passthrough to the user's real shell, filesystem commands, `child_process` execution from terminal input, or arbitrary command execution.
No changes to reward calculation, tier thresholds, redemption logic, equals counting, or local tracker behavior.
No changes to local state persistence under `~/.kitcode/state.json` or tracker metadata under `~/.kitcode/tracker.json`.
No campaign backend, login, claim flow, or remote telemetry.
No redesign of the React dashboard, setup gateway, admin view, or current `kitcode mini` panel.
No dashboard overlay version in the first implementation.

acceptance_criteria.summary: `kitcode terminal` is documented in CLI help, participates in command dispatch, and exits nonzero with the existing tracker-unavailable message when the local tracker is not running.
The command opens a separate Electron window centered in the primary display work area, with `resizable: true`, `movable: true`, and sensible minimum dimensions.
The local tracker serves a terminal HTML view, expected at `GET /terminal`, without changing existing `/mini`, `/api/summary`, `/api/events`, or reward endpoints.
The terminal UI uses English-only copy, displays a large Vim-inspired title such as `KITCODE TERMINAL`, and includes a terminal-style prompt and status/tab line.
The input accepts only safe KitCode terminal commands: `help`, `status`, `summary`, `rewards`, `dashboard`, `mini`, and `clear`; unknown commands do not execute anything and suggest `help`.
The terminal keeps input focused, Enter submits commands, Up/Down navigates command history, and `clear` clears the visible output history.
`status`, `summary`, and `rewards` render from existing local summary and reward contract fields without changing tracker, reward, local state, or API response shapes.

coverage_plan.summary: Run the CLI package build script after implementation so command, reward, snapshot, ledger, and syntax checks still pass.
Extend CLI command checks so help includes `terminal` and `kitcode terminal` fails with the tracker-unavailable message when no tracker is running.
Add or perform a focused smoke check that the terminal HTML includes the large title, prompt, supported command labels, and no real-shell execution hooks.
Run `kitcode track` and `kitcode terminal`, then verify centered opening, drag, resize, prompt focus, command history, safe command outputs, dashboard open, and no arbitrary shell execution.

risks.summary: A realistic terminal UI may make users expect real shell execution.
risks.mitigation: Keep `help`, unknown-command copy, and supported command outputs explicit that this is a KitCode terminal, not a system shell; never execute arbitrary input.

risks.summary: Frameless custom chrome can make native-feeling resize and drag behavior fragile.
risks.mitigation: Prefer a normal resizable Electron window or carefully limit draggable custom regions; keep minimum dimensions stable and test resize manually.

risks.summary: Adding a public CLI command and `GET /terminal` expands both CLI and local HTTP surface area.
risks.mitigation: Update CLI help, docs, command checks, local HTTP contract notes, and route smoke coverage together.

risks.summary: If Electron is unavailable and the terminal view opens in a browser tab, the layout still needs to look intentional.
risks.mitigation: Make `/terminal` responsive within browser dimensions while keeping the Electron default centered and terminal-like.

risks.summary: A resizable terminal can be shrunk enough to cause title, prompt, or output overlap.
risks.mitigation: Set minimum BrowserWindow dimensions and CSS min sizes that keep the title, status line, and prompt readable.

implementation_handoff.summary: Introduce a safe terminal-style KitCode surface as a separate resizable Electron window launched by `kitcode terminal`.
suggested_sequence: Add terminal URL/open helpers and a `terminal` command branch in `packages/kitcode-cli/bin/kitcode.mjs`, mirroring the server check behavior used by `mini`.
Create a terminal Electron entry that opens `http://host:port/terminal`, centers the BrowserWindow in `screen.getPrimaryDisplay().workArea`, and allows resize/move with minimum dimensions.
Create a terminal HTML renderer and serve it from `GET /terminal` in `packages/kitcode-cli/src/api.mjs`.
Implement the browser-side safe command engine using only local API fetches/window actions for supported KitCode commands.
Style the route as an English Vim-inspired terminal with a large `KITCODE TERMINAL` title, status/tab line, output history, and prompt.
Update README/help/contracts/checks for the new command and route.
Run CLI build/checks and perform the manual Electron terminal verification.
current_behavior_evidence: packages/kitcode-cli/bin/kitcode.mjs currently lists `dashboard` and `mini` in help and command dispatch, but no `terminal` command exists.
packages/kitcode-cli/bin/kitcode.mjs currently uses `isServerRunning` and `printTrackerNotRunning` for `dashboard` and `mini`, which should be reused for `terminal`.
packages/kitcode-cli/src/api.mjs currently serves `/mini`, `/api/summary`, `/api/events`, `/api/projects`, and reward redemption, but no `/terminal` route.
packages/kitcode-cli/src/mini-electron.mjs shows the existing Electron pattern for loading a local tracker URL into a BrowserWindow.
apps/web/src/components/header.tsx and apps/web/src/index.css show the existing terminal/Vim visual language that the terminal view should echo without redesigning the dashboard.
notes: Use English copy only.
The requested title treatment should be large like a real terminal/Vim surface, not a small modal heading.
Keep command execution local and safe; terminal input must never invoke the user's real shell.
The first implementation should be Electron-only for the launch surface; a dashboard overlay can wait.

goal: Add a macOS-first KitCode desktop pet whose project-owned visual resources are generated once during implementation with `$hatch-pet`, use #fc0a0a as the primary color, can be dragged anywhere on the desktop as a transparent overlay, stays pinned where dropped like Codex pet behavior, and is shown or hidden only through a PET toggle inside the KitCode Terminal window.

in: Use the two user-provided screenshots from 2026-07-10 as the visual source of truth: a soft 3D toy robot with a white rounded body, oversized rounded black CRT-style face screen, red side ear panels and trim, short rounded limbs, and a red KC chest badge.

Use #fc0a0a as the exact primary red for face pixels, KC badge, trim, highlights, and active interaction accents; retain white and near-black as the supporting neutral palette and do not reintroduce the former green primary.

Create production pet art with a transparent background and consistent character geometry across every animation frame; visual acceptance requires no visible redesign away from the reference character.

Provide at least rest, work/walk, blink, and celebrate animations matching the four states shown in the reference, with red pixel-screen expressions; retain the suggested terminal-expression language such as >_, curved blink eyes, {}, </>, a check mark, and 404 where contextually useful.

During implementation, invoke the installed `$hatch-pet` skill as a build-time asset-generation tool with both Kit Terminal reference images, the `3d-toy` style direction, the approved KC badge, and #fc0a0a palette constraint; do not hand-author or substitute a different mascot asset path before this grounded generation attempt is completed.

Promote only the final visually approved and deterministically validated Hatch output needed by KitCode into `packages/kitcode-cli/src/pet-assets/kit-terminal/`, including the final spritesheet and a compact local manifest; keep generation prompts, row strips, extracted frames, and temporary job state out of the published package.

Keep animation row/frame definitions and KitCode state mapping in project-owned runtime logic so idle, drag feedback, work, blink, celebrate, and offline behavior continue to work without Hatch, Codex, or files under the user's Codex home directory.
Launch the pet as a separate frameless, transparent, non-resizable, always-on-top Electron overlay with no panel, card, browser chrome, taskbar item, or mini-window background.

Allow the pet to be dragged across usable desktop work areas, remain stationary by default, stay pinned at the release position after drop, and stay clear of menu bars, docks, and taskbars through workArea clamping.
Allow direct dragging of the visible pet with a short appropriate drag/drop animation response, and keep transparent space click-through so the overlay does not obstruct normal desktop interaction.

Support macOS primary and secondary displays for the first version, including dragging between displays, clamping to a valid work area, and recovering to an available display after monitor topology changes.

Add a visible PET ON/OFF toggle to the KitCode Terminal chrome, available in terminal, compact, progress, and watch modes; the control defaults to OFF for each Terminal session and exposes synchronized `aria-pressed`, label, and Show pet/Hide pet tooltip state.

Make the Terminal Electron main process own the pet as a secondary BrowserWindow in the same app lifecycle: the first ON action creates and shows one pet window, subsequent ON actions reuse it, OFF hides it and pauses movement/animation, and ON after OFF resumes it at its last valid position in the current session.
Close or destroy the pet window when the Terminal window closes; closing Terminal must leave the local tracker running, while reopening Terminal starts a new session with PET OFF.

When `/terminal` is opened in the browser fallback without the Electron preload bridge, keep the PET control disabled and label it as requiring the desktop Terminal instead of attempting to create an overlay.

Use the existing `/api/summary` initial data and `/api/events` SSE stream so tracker activity drives work/idle behavior, a ready reward triggers celebrate, and disconnect/reconnect produces a quiet offline/sleeping response.
Keep the pet renderer sandboxed and expose only allowlisted Electron actions needed for Terminal-owned show/hide state, drag behavior, visibility synchronization, and lifecycle control.
Add focused static checks plus manual native and visual QA for overlay behavior, reference fidelity, animation states, multi-monitor drag placement, input pass-through, and resource use.
out: Do not restore the removed standalone `kitcode mini` command or `/mini` route, and do not implement the pet as another terminal view-mode preset.
Do not use a full-screen transparent window that can intercept the whole desktop; move a tightly bounded transparent pet window instead.
Do not redesign the Kit Terminal robot into a different mascot, pixel-art-only character, flat icon, animal, or generic terminal logo.
Do not change reward thresholds, redemption behavior, equals counting, tracker timing, source snapshots, or the existing summary response shape.
Do not add a campaign backend, account, remote telemetry, or source-code upload.
Do not add persistent pet position, multiple skins, accessories, feeding, leveling, or other pet-game systems in the first version.
Do not promise equivalent Windows or Linux overlay polish in this macOS-first version; preserve a portable structure for later work.
Do not allow pet or Terminal input to execute arbitrary system-shell commands.
Do not add a public `kitcode pet` command, a safe-shell `pet` command, command-line pet options, an independent pet process, or a separately launched pet application.
Do not persist PET ON/OFF state or last position across Terminal sessions in the first version; session-only state is sufficient.
Do not require pet-side close, pause, or quit controls as the primary control surface; visibility and lifecycle are owned by the Terminal PET toggle.
Do not expose Hatch as a KitCode CLI command, runtime feature, user-facing dependency, pet marketplace, pet selector, or generic custom-pet system.
Do not install the production KitCode pet into `~/.codex/pets`, read runtime assets from `$CODEX_HOME`, or require the `$hatch-pet` skill on an end user's machine.
Do not publish Hatch prompts, image-generation manifests, layout guides, intermediate atlases, raw row strips, extracted frames, or other generation-only artifacts inside the npm package.

acceptance_criteria.summary: The delivered pet visibly matches the supplied Kit Terminal robot reference in silhouette, proportions, white toy-like body, rounded black CRT face, red side panels and trim, short limbs, and KC chest badge; visual review rejects any obvious character redesign or frame-to-frame identity drift.
The pet uses #fc0a0a as the exact primary color for screen pixels and red brand details, with no green primary remaining in the pet surface.

Rest, work/walk, blink, and celebrate are distinct animated states that preserve one consistent robot and reproduce the reference's red terminal-face expression language; celebrate has a clearly more energetic pose/effect than idle states.

Implementation invokes `$hatch-pet` with both supplied Kit Terminal references and the approved 3D-toy/KC/#fc0a0a constraints, completes the skill's visual and deterministic QA gates, and promotes the selected final atlas rather than treating Hatch as a KitCode product feature.

The approved spritesheet, compact manifest, and KitCode animation mapping are stored under the CLI package source and are sufficient to render the pet without reading `~/.codex/pets`, `$CODEX_HOME`, Hatch run folders, or generation intermediates at runtime.

The npm package dry-run includes the final Kit Terminal spritesheet, local manifest, and runtime animation module while excluding Hatch prompts, job manifests, row strips, extracted frames, and other generation-only artifacts.

The pet appears directly on the desktop in a tightly bounded transparent, frameless, non-resizable, always-on-top Electron window with no visible card, background, title bar, Dock icon, or taskbar entry.

While visible, the Terminal-owned pet stays stationary by default, can be dragged outside the Terminal bounds across valid desktop work areas, gives short drag/drop feedback, stays pinned at the release position, and never settles outside the visible usable bounds.

The visible character can be dragged and released while transparent overlay space remains click-through; normal interaction with applications behind the pet is not blocked outside the character hit area.
On macOS the pet can be moved between displays, uses each display's workArea, and returns to an available visible work area if a display is disconnected or its geometry changes.

The Terminal chrome exposes an accessible PET toggle in terminal, compact, progress, and watch modes; it defaults OFF, ON creates or reuses and shows one pet window, OFF hides it and pauses movement/animation, and the control state stays synchronized with the actual pet window.

The pet is a secondary BrowserWindow owned by the active Terminal Electron app, never a separate CLI process or application; closing Terminal closes the pet but leaves the tracker running, and reopening Terminal starts with PET OFF.
When `/terminal` runs without the Electron preload bridge, the PET toggle is disabled with clear desktop-Terminal-required labeling and no overlay launch attempt occurs.

The pet reads existing summary/SSE data without changing its contract: active tracking selects work behavior, idle selects rest, a ready tier selects celebrate, and connection loss selects a quiet offline or sleeping state until reconnection.
The standalone mini command and route remain removed, all current Terminal view modes continue to work, and tracker/reward calculations and persisted local state remain unchanged.

coverage_plan.summary: Use `$hatch-pet` during implementation to generate the Kit Terminal pet from the two reference images and retain only a final output that passes the skill's required visual, atlas, transparency, motion, and direction checks before promotion into KitCode source.

Add a focused resource check that validates the project-local spritesheet and manifest, required KitCode animation mappings, package-relative asset resolution, and absence of runtime `$CODEX_HOME` or Hatch-run-folder dependencies.
Inspect the npm dry-run file list and verify that final pet resources and runtime logic are included while generation-only Hatch artifacts are excluded.
Run the complete CLI package build so existing command, Terminal mode, reward, ledger, snapshot, integration, and syntax checks continue to pass.

Add a focused check for the Terminal PET toggle in every view mode, default OFF state, accessible pressed/tooltip state, allowlisted show/hide IPC, one-window reuse, browser-fallback disablement, Terminal-owned lifecycle, transparent overlay options, #fc0a0a token, required animation states, and existing summary/SSE usage.

Render the transparent pet at rest, work/walk, blink, and celebrate states and compare each capture against the supplied Kit Terminal reference at equivalent scale; do not accept visible changes to character geometry, badge, face construction, or palette.

On macOS run KitCode Terminal, then verify PET defaults OFF, ON creates/shows one overlay, OFF hides it, repeated toggles reuse one window and resume the session position, closing Terminal closes the pet but not the tracker, and stationary placement, drag/drop feedback, click-through, Spaces behavior, and resource use remain correct.
Verify dragging and pinned placement on two displays, disconnect/reconnect recovery, tracker active/idle transitions, SSE loss/reconnect, and ready-tier celebration without changing reward data.

risks.summary: Generated or hand-authored animation frames may drift away from the reference robot's face shape, body proportions, KC badge, or material treatment, making a claimed 100% match visibly inconsistent.
risks.mitigation: Persist the supplied references at implementation start, establish one approved transparent master character, derive every frame from that master, and require four-state side-by-side visual review before acceptance.

risks.summary: The two current screenshot paths are under macOS TemporaryItems and may disappear before implementation or later visual verification.
risks.mitigation: At the beginning of implementation, copy the still-available user-provided references into a durable project-local reference location without altering them; if unavailable, request the originals again before creating pet art.

risks.summary: Electron mouse-ignore behavior applies at window level, while the pet must be draggable without transparent pixels blocking the desktop.
risks.mitigation: Keep bounds tight, implement explicit visible-character hit testing with controlled ignore-mouse switching, and manually verify both drag acquisition and pass-through over transparent corners.

risks.summary: Native drag/drop placement can feel wrong if movement feedback persists too long or the pet keeps moving after release.
risks.mitigation: Keep placement user-driven, use a short bounded drag feedback timer, return to idle after drop, and measure idle and drag resource use during native QA.

risks.summary: Always-on-top level, full-screen Spaces, Dock placement, scaling, and monitor removal can change where the pet is visible or leave it off-screen.
risks.mitigation: Use display workArea and scale-aware bounds, listen for display changes, clamp after every topology change, and test normal desktops plus full-screen Spaces on the supported macOS version.

risks.summary: Repeated toggle actions, renderer reloads, or an unexpected pet-window close could create duplicate BrowserWindows or leave the Terminal toggle out of sync with actual visibility.
risks.mitigation: Keep one main-process pet-window reference, make show/hide IPC idempotent, send visibility updates back to the renderer, clear the reference on close, and cover repeated toggle plus renderer reload behavior.

risks.summary: A naive integration could leave the pet dependent on `~/.codex/pets`, Hatch working directories, generated prompts, or a locally installed skill, causing packaged KitCode installs to lose their visual resources.
risks.mitigation: Treat Hatch as implementation-only tooling, copy the final approved spritesheet and compact manifest into package-owned source, keep animation mapping in KitCode modules, and verify the npm dry-run contents plus runtime path resolution.

implementation_handoff.summary: Use `$hatch-pet` once to produce the visual asset, then implement the pet as a Terminal-owned secondary desktop overlay controlled only by an accessible PET toggle inside the KitCode Terminal chrome; no pet CLI or safe-shell command is added.

asset_generation.purpose: Implementation-time generation and QA only; it is not a KitCode runtime feature or user-facing command.
inputs: Both user-provided Kit Terminal screenshots after they are preserved at durable project-local paths.
Pet name `Kit Terminal`, style preset `3d-toy`, approved readable KC chest badge, and #fc0a0a primary color constraint.
Stable identity notes covering the white rounded toy body, black CRT face screen, red side panels and trim, short limbs, and terminal-expression language.
asset_generation.required_output: One final transparent, visually approved, deterministically validated spritesheet plus a compact manifest suitable for KitCode's package-local renderer.
asset_generation.runtime_boundary: Do not install or resolve the production pet from `~/.codex/pets` or `$CODEX_HOME`; do not ship Hatch prompts, manifests, intermediates, scripts, or skill dependencies.

suggested_sequence: Preserve the two user-provided reference screenshots from their TemporaryItems paths in a durable project-local reference location before they disappear; if either source is unavailable, stop asset creation and request it again.

goal: Fix the KitCode desktop pet so it behaves like the Codex pet: clicking the pet grabs it for drag instead of clicking through to apps behind it, dropping pins it in place, and default animation stays quiet and state-driven instead of looping arbitrary motion.

in: Make the visible pet area reliably receive mouse input so users can click and drag the pet immediately from the desktop overlay.
Remove the current mouse-ignore deadlock where the native pet window forwards events to apps behind it before the renderer can detect interactive pixels.
Prioritize Codex-like drag behavior over perfect per-pixel click-through inside the pet's tight 192x208 overlay bounds.
Keep the overlay tightly bounded to the pet asset; the desktop must remain normally clickable outside the pet window.
Keep `-webkit-app-region: drag` or equivalent native drag support so drag works without adding an in-pet command, button, or separate control surface.
After drop, keep the pet pinned at the released position for the current Terminal session and reuse that position across PET OFF/ON toggles.
Keep display workArea clamping and display-change recovery so a dragged pet cannot remain off-screen after monitor changes.
Make default animation quiet: opening may wave once, idle may blink lightly, drag/drop may show a short feedback animation, and reward-ready may celebrate.

Stop using active tracking or generic online state to loop full-body `working` animation continuously; active tracking may update a subtle face/state expression only if it does not look like arbitrary movement.
Keep summary/SSE reads and reward contracts unchanged; this requirement changes pet presentation and input behavior only.
Update focused checks so they catch click-through drag regressions, pinned drop behavior, quiet default animation policy, and no new `kitcode pet` command.
out: No new CLI command, safe-shell command, pet palette, pet marketplace, Hatch runtime dependency, or standalone pet process.
No persistent pet position across Terminal sessions; position remains session-only.
No full-screen transparent overlay and no desktop-wide input capture.
No reward math, tracker, local API response shape, persisted state, or campaign backend changes.
No attempt to guarantee perfect per-pixel click-through inside the tight pet window in this correction; that can be revisited later with native hit-test work if needed.
No redesign or regeneration of the Kit Terminal pet art unless the existing frames cannot support the needed quiet/drag feedback states.

acceptance_criteria.summary: When PET is ON, clicking the visible pet overlay starts native drag instead of activating whatever app/content is behind the pet.
After the user releases a drag, the pet remains at the dropped position, does not auto-walk away, and PET OFF/ON reuses that session position.
Only the tight pet BrowserWindow can intercept input; desktop/app interaction outside the 192x208 pet overlay remains unaffected, with no full-screen transparent capture window.

Visible pet defaults to a calm idle state with only occasional blink; opening, drag/drop, reward-ready, offline, and reconnecting states have explicit animation reasons, and active tracking no longer causes continuous arbitrary full-body looping.
The pet continues reading existing `/api/summary` and `/api/events` data without changing reward, tracker, local HTTP, or persisted state contracts.
The PET toggle remains the only control surface; no standalone `kitcode pet` command, safe-shell `pet` command, or independent pet application is introduced.

risks.summary: Electron mouse forwarding and native drag acquisition conflict: forwarding events lets users click apps behind the pet, but it also prevents the pet renderer from receiving the first event needed to start drag.
risks.mitigation: For this correction, prioritize Codex-like drag reliability and keep the overlay tightly bounded; defer perfect per-pixel click-through inside the pet box unless native hit-test work is explicitly requested.

risks.summary: Making the pet quiet can either feel lifeless or still feel noisy if the active-tracking state loops too often.
risks.mitigation: Use idle/blink as the default, reserve stronger loops for reward-ready or explicit transient actions, and manually QA perceived motion with tracker active and inactive.

risks.summary: The Codex runner has previously timed out before Electron `app.ready`, so full native verification may still require running the harness in a normal macOS Terminal.
risks.mitigation: Keep static/build checks deterministic in CI-like contexts and document the native command for local macOS verification.

implementation_handoff.summary: Correct the pet overlay input and animation policy so the first user click grabs the pet for drag, drop pins it, and idle behavior is calm and explainable.
suggested_sequence: Change the native pet BrowserWindow input mode so the visible pet can receive the first click/drag instead of forwarding it to apps behind the pet.
Remove or simplify the renderer alpha-hit-test path if it no longer participates in first-click drag acquisition.
Keep the window size bounded to the pet dimensions and preserve session-only lastPosition reuse plus display workArea clamping.
Adjust the animation decision policy so active tracking does not continuously loop full-body working motion; default visible state should settle to idle plus occasional blink.
Update focused static and native checks for the new click/drag and quiet-animation contract, then run the package build and manual macOS QA.
current_behavior_evidence: packages/kitcode-cli/src/pet-electron.mjs currently calls `setIgnoreMouseEvents(true, {forward: true})` when the pet window is created, so the first click can pass through to the app behind the pet.

packages/kitcode-cli/src/pet-window.mjs currently tries to call `setInteractive` from `mousemove` after alpha hit-testing, but ignored mouse events can prevent that mousemove from reaching the renderer.
packages/kitcode-cli/src/pet-window.mjs currently maps active tracking summaries to `working`, which can make the pet loop motion even when the user expects it to stand still.
packages/kitcode-cli/src/pet-electron.mjs already stores `lastPosition` from native move events and can reuse that as the session-pinned drop location.
notes: This is a correction to the existing `kit-terminal-desktop-pet` work, not a new user-facing pet command or Hatch feature.
The product priority is Codex-like drag reliability. Perfect transparent-pixel pass-through inside the tight pet window is explicitly lower priority for this correction.
